rationale: DevOps engineers and engineering managers at software companies running macOS CI/CD — a named role with real budget authority — are genuinely losing money each month on cloud CI costs, and at least some are already doing this math manually (concrete buyer signal). The tool is a pure-math calculator wrapped in a simple form: fully buildable as a Claude prompt + landing page + optional Stripe, and fully autonomous to operate once live. The main risk is willingness to pay for a calculator (vs. just doing it in a spreadsheet), which keeps WTP at the floor; a free tier with a $29 paid export/team version is the realistic monetisation path.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a CI Cost Break-Even Calculator: users enter their monthly GitHub Actions minutes, macOS runner price per minute, and hardware cost, and get a payback timeline plus a recommendation. The factory builds it as a Claude-powered form (inputs → structured calculation → formatted report) hosted on a simple landing page with a Stripe payment link for a one-time $19–29 'detailed report + CSV export' upsell; no coding by the operator. Outreach targets DevOps/platform engineering communities: a post in r/devops, GitHub Discussions, and a cold-email sequence to engineering managers scraped from LinkedIn (operator approves each send batch). Once live, the calculator runs 24/7 without involvement — Claude handles the computation, Stripe handles billing, and a templated follow-up email is sent automatically; the operator's only recurring touch is approving outreach batches and reviewing weekly revenue reports.
notes: All build_gates pass: operational_autonomy=9, buildability_with_ai=9, buyer_clarity=7, willingness_to_pay=5. Main risk: a free spreadsheet template competes directly — position on speed and shareable report output.
